transcript: Yesterday, I attended a new musical called We Are Your Robots. Written and performed by a small band of robots featuring Ethan Lipton as the frontman, this is an 80-minute robot presentation where the robots and the audience learn about each other. It’s a humorous look at our codependent relationship with technology and an endearing nod to what makes us human such as our consciousness and our sense of uncertainty. To be honest, I encountered this piece at a time where I'm a little burnt out and turned off by explicit discussions of technology in general, so that clouded my experience a bit but it was still pretty enjoyable. The comedic tone of the piece, the design elements, and the music itself all had a charmingly retro feel that was fitting to the themes, and the music was definitely the highlight for me. All the musicians were fantastic and the songs were quite earwormy. We Are Your Robots is running through December 8th at Theater for a New Audience. With that, another program for my collection.
